Rashi on Ketubot 61b:10:1.english: Men of leisure - [This is] explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:10:2.english: The donkey drivers - Who go out to the villages to bring grain to sell in the market.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:10:3.english: The camel drivers - Merchants of bundles who bring [them] on camels from a distant place.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:10:4.english: The sailors - [They] set sail to the Great Sea, to the ends of the earth.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:11:1.english: From a woman who gives birth to a female - Who waits two weeks from marital relations.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:12:1.hebrew: נגמרו מיולדת נקבה - כיון דאשכחן אורח ארעא לשהות כל כך, אין לנו לכופו להוציא:
Rashi on Ketubot 61b:12:1.english: Let them derive [it] from a woman who gave birth [to] a female - Since we find [that it is] the way of the world to wait so long, we have no [grounds] to compel him to divorce [her].

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:12:2.hebrew: ה"ג - אי מיולדת גמרי, הכי נמי:
Rashi on Ketubot 61b:12:2.english: This is the reading - If they derive [it] from a woman who gave birth, indeed so.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:13:1.english: A common matter - Anger, when he becomes angry with his wife and imposes a vow upon her.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:13:2.hebrew: ממידי דשכיח - נדות, לאפוקי לידה דלא שכיח כולי האי:
Rashi on Ketubot 61b:13:2.english: From a common matter - [Namely,] menstruation, to the exclusion of childbirth, which is not so common.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:13:3.hebrew: מידי דהוא גרים לה - נדר האיש גורם לה לשהות, וכן לידה על ידו באה לה, לאפוקי נדה דממילא. ויש לנו ללמוד מן הדומה [אפילו לא שכיח כולי האי]:
Rashi on Ketubot 61b:13:3.english: A matter that he causes her - The husband's vow causes her to wait, and likewise childbirth comes to her through him, excluding [the case of] a menstruating woman, which [comes] on its own. And we should derive [it] from what is similar [even if it is not so common].

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:14:1.hebrew: אפי' בסתם נמי ימתין - לב"ש שתי שבתות, ולב"ה שבת אחת:
Rashi on Ketubot 61b:14:1.english: Even [with regard to] an unspecified [vow] he should also wait - For Beit Shammai, two weeks, and for Beit Hillel, one week.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:14:2.hebrew: שמא - בתוך הזמן ילמוד למצוא פתח חרטה, לומר אדעתא דהכי לא נדרי, ויתיר לו חכם נדרו:
Rashi on Ketubot 61b:14:2.english: Perhaps - within the [waiting] time he will learn to find an opening of regret, to say, "With this in mind, I did not vow," and a sage will annul his vow for him.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:15:1.hebrew: מליהנות לו עד ל' יום - קונם את נהנית לי עד ל' יום. ולא הדירה מהנאת תשמיש, דהא לא חייל, משום דמשועבד לה. וגבי מזונות נמי, מוקמינן ליה לקמן (כתובות ד' ע:) באומר לה: "צאי מעשה ידיך למזונותיך", ופרנס — משום דלא ספקא. ואית דמוקמא כגון שהוא מן הגמלי' או מן הספנים, שאין לכופו בשביל תשמיש. ולאו מילתא היא, דהא מוקמא לקמן, אכולהו קתני מתני' לענין מדיר שבוע אחת:
Rashi on Ketubot 61b:15:1.english: From benefiting from him for up to thirty days - [That is, he said:] "Konam [forbidden as a vow] is any benefit you derive from me for up to thirty days." And he did not vow [to prohibit] her from the benefit of marital relations, for [such a vow] does not take effect because he is obligated to her [for marital relations]. And regarding sustenance as well, we establish it later (Ketubot 70b) as [referring to] one who says to her, "Dedicate your handiwork to your sustenance," and [he must appoint] a trustee because [her handiwork] does not suffice [for her full support]. And there are those who establish [the Mishnah] as [referring to a case] where he is one of the camel drivers or one of the sailors, whom one cannot compel [to divorce] on account of marital relations. But this is not [a valid] statement, for it is established later [that] the Mishnah teaches [its ruling] regarding all of them with respect to one who vows for one week:

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:15:2.hebrew: יעמיד פרנס - שיזון אותה. והתם פריך: ואטו פרנס לאו שליחותיה עביד?:
Rashi on Ketubot 61b:15:2.english: He must appoint a trustee - who will sustain her. And there, [the Gemara] asks: "Does a trustee not act as his agent?"

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:16:1.english: Marital relations are not possible through a trustee.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:16:2.english: And if it were stated regarding this [case] - [That is, regarding the case of prohibiting her] from deriving benefit from him.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:16:3.english: In this [case] Shmuel said - Because [it] is possible through a trustee.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:1:1.english: Whose face turned pale - His face was downcast, for he craved the food.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:1:10.english: On his nostrils - We do not read [this in the text].

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:1:11.hebrew: הכא מי בדקיתו - כלומר, בדקתם את חתיכה הזו:
Rashi on Ketubot 61b:1:11.english: Did you check here? - That is to say, did you check this piece?

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:1:12.english: They checked [and] found [it] - A miracle was performed for him.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:1:13.english: That was hovering over him - [Over] Mar Zutra.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:1:2.hebrew: א"ל - אטורנגא לרב אשי:
Rashi on Ketubot 61b:1:2.english: He said to him - The *aturanga* [chief butler, said] to Rav Ashi.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:1:3.english: You have spoiled the meal - The king will not eat [from it] from now on.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:1:4.english: They said to him - The king's officers [said]: "Why did you do this?"

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:1:5.english: He said to them - Rav Ashi.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:1:6.hebrew: דעביד הכי פסיל למיכל למלכא - העושה מאכל כזה, אין ראוי שיאכל המלך מאכל מידו:
Rashi on Ketubot 61b:1:6.english: [One] who does thus is unfit for the king to eat [from] - One who makes such food, it is not fitting that the king should eat food from his hand.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:1:7.hebrew: דבר אחר חזאי ביה - בשר של חזיר מצורע, ובלשון לעז קורין לו שורשמי"ן:
Rashi on Ketubot 61b:1:7.english: I saw something else in it - Meat of a leprous pig, and in the vernacular [Old French] they call it "sursemin" [measly].

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:1:8.english: He took his finger - Rav Ashi took the cook's finger:

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:1:9.english: He placed [it] on it - On one of the pieces.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:2:1.hebrew: פלי - מבקע, והרבה יש לו דומים במסכת נדה (דף כא:) דפלי פלויי:
Rashi on Ketubot 61b:2:1.english: [He] split [them] open - Splits [them] open; and it has many similar [usages] in Tractate Niddah (21b), [such as] "that he splits [it] open" (d'falei faluyei).

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:2:2.english: Saliva that causes anguish - Saliva that builds up inside the mouth due to the craving for something eaten in front of him, [while] he does not eat of it.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:2:3.hebrew: עד דזג - נפחו פניה וכריסה ונעשו כזכוכית, שכן דרכי הנפוחים:
Rashi on Ketubot 61b:2:3.english: Until she became translucent - Her face and her belly swelled and became like glass, for such is the way of those who are swollen.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:2:4.english: Spit [it] out, cast [it] away - Spit [and] throw [it] away.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:3:2.hebrew: בהמתו - סוס וחמור, שהן מזויינין וצוהלים לרביעה; אבל בקר אינו להוט אחר רביעת אשה ואין יצרו ניכר כל כך, לפיכך אין אשה נסתית לו. ואני שמעתי: בקרו — נקבות, בהמתו — זכרים:
Rashi on Ketubot 61b:3:2.english: His animals - A horse and a donkey, which are well-endowed and neigh for mating; whereas cattle are not eager for mating with a woman and their [sexual] urge is not so noticeable, therefore a woman is not enticed by them. And I have heard: "his cattle" [refers to] females, [and] "his animals" [refers to] males.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:3:3.hebrew: משרבט - פושטן כמין שרביט עד שנעשין גדולות, ובלשונינו נקרא אשא"ש, ע"י שהיא צריכה לשרות החוט תמיד ברוק:
Rashi on Ketubot 61b:3:3.english: Stretches out [the lips] - [The flax] stretches them like a rod until they become large, and in our language [Old French] it is called *ashash*, because she needs to constantly soak the thread with saliva.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:5:1.hebrew: שפוד שפחות וגומות - סימני הלכות הן: שפוד במסכת ביצה, שפחות כאן, גומות במסכת נדה, בלורית במסכת עבודה זרה, אפר מקלה במסכת מכות, גבינה במסכת עבודה זרה. תלת מנייהו מתני' — שפחות ובלורי' וגבינה — ותלת מנייהו שמעתת', ופרשינהו רב מלכיו ורב מלכיא:
Rashi on Ketubot 61b:5:1.english: Skewer, maidservants, and follicles - They are mnemonics for legal rulings: "skewer" in tractate Beitzah; "maidservants" here [in Ketubot]; "follicles" in tractate Niddah; "forelock" [belorit] in tractate Avodah Zarah; "wood ashes" in tractate Makkot; [and] "cheese" in tractate Avodah Zarah. Three of them are [stated on] Mishnayot — maidservants, forelock, and cheese — and three of them are Amoraic traditions [shema'tata], and Rav Malkiyu and Rav Malkiya explained them.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:7:1.hebrew: רב פפא - אסימנא דרב מלכיו פליג, דקאמר שפחות רב מלכיו, ליתא, דכל מתני' ומתניתא דהכא רב מלכיא פרשינהו. אבל שמעתתא דאמר ברב מלכיו, מודינא לך:
Rashi on Ketubot 61b:7:1.english: Rav Pappa - He disagrees with the mnemonic regarding Rav Malkiyyu: what he said, [that] "maidservants" [was stated by] Rav Malkiyyu, is not [so], for Rav Malkiya explained all [the teachings on] the Mishnah and Baraita here. However, [regarding] the [amoraic] statements that he said [were] by Rav Malkiyyu, I agree with you.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:7:2.english: And your mnemonic - So that you do not switch [them] in the textual version.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:7:3.hebrew: מתניתא מלכתא - לגבי שמעתא הויא מתניתא מלכתא, דהא מינה מותבינן תיובתא לשמעתא. וסימניך: מלכיא לשון נקבה, אבל מלכיו לשון זכר:
Rashi on Ketubot 61b:7:3.english: A baraita is a queen - Relative to an Amoraic statement, a baraita is a queen, for from it we raise a refutation against an Amoraic statement. And your mnemonic [is]: Malkiya is a feminine form, whereas Malkiyyu is a masculine form.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:8:1.hebrew: היינו ת"ק - רבי אליעזר; מה לי לידי שעמום, מה לי לידי זימה:
Rashi on Ketubot 61b:8:1.english: This is [the same as] the first Tanna - [namely,] Rabbi Eliezer; what difference is it to me [whether it leads] to idiocy, [or] what difference is it to me [whether it leads] to licentiousness?

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:8:2.hebrew: דמיטללא בגורייתא קיטנייתא ונדרשיר - משחקת בכלבים דקים, ושחוק שקורין אישקקי"ש. לידי זימה איכא, לידי שיעמום ליכא, דאין שיעמום אלא ביושב ותוהא ובטל לגמרי:
Rashi on Ketubot 61b:8:2.english: When she plays with small dogs or nadrashir - [She] plays with small dogs, and [with] a game called eschecs [chess]. [In this case, leading] to licentiousness is present, [while leading] to idiocy is not present, for idiocy only [occurs] in one who sits, stares [vacantly], and is completely idle.

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:9:1.hebrew: המדיר את אשתו - כגון דאמר: "יאסר הנאת תשמישך עלי", אבל "הנאת תשמישי עליך" לא מיתסרא, דהא משועבד לה, דכתיב: "ועונתה לא יגרע". והכי מוקמינן בנדרים, בפרק ואלו נדרים (נדרים דף פא:):
Rashi on Ketubot 61b:9:1.english: One who vows [regarding] his wife - For example, where he said, "May the benefit of marital relations with you be forbidden to me." However, [if he said,] "the benefit of marital relations with me [be forbidden] to you," it does not become forbidden, because he is obligated to her, as it is written: "Her conjugal rights he shall not diminish." And so we establish [this] in Nedarim, in the chapter [entitled] Ve'eilu Nedarim (Nedarim 81b).

Rashi on Ketubot 61b:9:2.hebrew: ב"ש אומרים שתי שבתות - אם הדירה ב' שבתות, תמתין; ואם יותר, יוציא ויתן כתובה:
Rashi on Ketubot 61b:9:2.english: Beit Shammai say: Two weeks - If he bound her by a vow [for] two weeks, she waits; and if [for] more, he must divorce [her] and pay [her] ketubah.

Tosafot on Ketubot 61b:10:1.hebrew: התלמידים יוצאין שלא ברשות ל' יום והפועלים שבת אחת - פי' ר"י, דאתא לאשמועינן דאף על גב דמנהגם היה ללמוד ולעשות מלאכה בעירם, ועונה האמורה בתור' לתלמיד מע"ש לע"ש כדאמרי' בגמ', ולפועלים שתים בשבת כדקתני סיפא — אפ"ה יכולים לשנות ממנהגם ולצאת: תלמידים ל' יום, ופועלים שבת אחת:
Tosafot on Ketubot 61b:10:1.english: Students may leave without permission for thirty days, and laborers for one week - Ri explained that [the Mishnah] comes to teach us that even though their custom was to study and to do work in their own town, and the [conjugal] interval stated in the Torah for a student is from Shabbat eve to Shabbat eve, as we say in the Gemara, and for laborers [it is] twice a week, as the latter clause [of the Mishnah] teaches — nevertheless, they may deviate from their custom and go out: students for thirty days, and laborers for one week.

Tosafot on Ketubot 61b:2:1.hebrew: לא ליתן תבן לפני בהמתו ולא ליתן תבן לפני בקרו - דשניהם אינה מחוייבת, כדתניא בפרק בתרא דנדרים (דף פא:): "דברים שבינה לבין אחרים אינו מיפר. כיצד? קונם שאני עושה לפי אבא, לפי אביך, לפי אחי, לפי אחיך, שלא אתן תבן לפני בהמתך, שלא אתן תבן לפני בקרך — אינו יכול להפר":
Tosafot on Ketubot 61b:2:1.english: "Not to place straw before his animal, and not to place straw before his cattle" - For she is not obligated [to perform] either of them, as it is taught in the last chapter of Nedarim (81b): "Matters between her and others, he cannot nullify [her vows]. How so? [If she says:] 'Konam [that] I will not do [work] for my father's mouth, for your father's mouth, for my brother's mouth, for your brother's mouth, [or] that I will not place straw before your animal, [or] that I will not place straw before your cattle' — he cannot nullify [the vow]."

Tosafot on Ketubot 61b:2:2.hebrew: יכול יהא חלב מהלכי שתים טמא ודם מהלכי שתים טמא - בת"כ גרסי' בשר במקום דם, וקאמר: ת"ל "זה" — אוציא חלב שאינו נוהג בכל — פירוש, דחלב בהמה טהורה מותר — ולא אוציא את הבשר שהוא נוהג בכל, שאף בבהמה טהורה אסור בשר מן החי? ת"ל "זה טמא": זה בלא תעשה על אכילתו, ואין בשר מהלכי שתים כו'. ואור"י דבין לפי ספרים שלנו, דדריש מ"הוא" היתר חלב ודם, ובין לת"כ, דדריש מ"זה", אתי שפיר, דמצי למעוטי חלב בשר ודם כולהו מחד קרא, כמו שמצינו בכמה מקומות דממעטין מחד קרא כמה דברים, כדאשכחן בפרק הנהנה מן ההקדש (מעילה יח:) דכמה פעמים קאמר "תמעול מעל" ריבה. ופליגא השתא אברייתא דפרק דם שחיטה (כריתות כ: ושם), דממעט דם מהלכי שתים מדכתיב "לעוף ולבהמה". ויש ספרים דממעטין חלב מדכתיב "הוא", ודם מדכתיב "זה". ותימה לר"י: דמנא לן לאוקמא אדם? דסברא הוא יותר לאוקמא אבשר, ולהתיר בשר מדם, דאין איסור בשר נוהג בכל אלא מחיים, אבל דם איסורו נוהג בכל, בין מחיים בין לאחר מיתה. ואור"י דאי הוה גריס בשמעתין בשר במקום דם הוה אתי שפיר, דמ"זה" ומ"הוא" ממעטינן חלב ובשר, ומההוא קרא דכריתות ממעטינן דם. וא"ת: וכיון דממעטינן דם מההוא קרא דכריתות, אמאי איצטריך קרא למישרי חלב? השתא דם מותר, חלב לא כ"ש? וי"ל: דמההוא קרא דכריתות לא מצי למישרי דם לגמרי, דלא ממעטינן ליה אלא מאיסור דם, אבל מאיסור טמא לא ממעטינן ליה; והואיל ונתמעט מאיסור דם, השתא דם וחלב שוין:
Tosafot on Ketubot 61b:2:2.english: Could it be that the milk of bipedal [creatures] is impure, and the blood of bipedal [creatures] is impure - In Torat Kohanim we read "flesh" in place of "blood," and it says: Scripture teaches "this" — should I exclude milk, which does not apply in all cases (meaning, that the milk of a kosher animal is permitted), and not exclude flesh, which applies in all cases, for even in a kosher animal, flesh [torn] from a living [animal] is forbidden? Scripture teaches "this is impure" — this [is subject to] a negative prohibition regarding its consumption, whereas the flesh of bipedal [creatures] is not, etc. And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that both according to our texts, which expound the permissibility of milk and blood from "it," and according to Torat Kohanim, which expounds [it] from "this," it works out well: for one can exclude milk, flesh, and blood — all of them — from a single verse, just as we find in several places that we exclude several things from a single verse, as we find in the chapter HaNeheneh min HaHekdesh (Me'ilah 18b), where several times it says: "tim'ol ma'al" ('commits a trespass') is an inclusion. And [this] now disagrees with the baraita in the chapter Dam Shechitah (Keritot 20b and there), which excludes the blood of bipedal [creatures] from what is written, "to fowl and to beast." And there are texts that exclude milk from what is written "it," and blood from what is written "this." And this is astonishing to Rabbeinu Yitzchak: From where do we [know] to establish [the exclusion] as referring to blood? For it is more logical to establish it as referring to flesh, and to permit flesh rather than blood, since the prohibition of flesh does not apply in all cases, [applying] only during [the animal's] lifetime, whereas the prohibition of blood applies in all cases, both during [its] lifetime and after death. And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that if one were to read in our sugya "flesh" in place of "blood," it would work out well: for from "this" and from "it" we exclude milk and flesh, and from that verse in Keritot we exclude blood. And if you say: Since we exclude blood from that verse in Keritot, why was a verse needed to permit milk? Now [that] blood is permitted, is milk not all the more so [permitted]? And one can say [in answer]: From that verse in Keritot, one cannot permit blood completely, for we only exclude it from the prohibition of blood, but we do not exclude it from the prohibition of an impure [creature]; and since it has been excluded from the prohibition of blood, now blood and milk are equal.

Tosafot on Ketubot 61b:3:1.hebrew: לא ליתן תבן לפני בהמתו ולא ליתן תבן לפני בקרו - דשניהם אינה מחוייבת, כדתניא בפרק בתרא דנדרים (דף פא:): דברים שבינה לבין אחרים — אינו מיפר; כיצד? "קונם שאני עושה לפי אבא, לפי אביך, לפי אחי, לפי אחיך, שלא אתן תבן לפני בהמתך, שלא אתן תבן לפני בקרך" — אינו יכול להפר:
Tosafot on Ketubot 61b:3:1.english: "Not to place straw before his animals, and not to place straw before his cattle" - For she is not obligated in either of them, as it is taught [in a baraita] in the last chapter of Nedarim (81b): [Regarding] matters that are between her and others, he cannot annul [her vows]. How so? [If she vows,] "Konam [be any benefit from what] I produce for [my] father, for your father, for [my] brother, [or] for your brother; [or] that I will not place straw before your animals, [or] that I will not place straw before your cattle" — he cannot annul [it].

Tosafot on Ketubot 61b:3:2.hebrew: וה"מ בכיתנא רומאה - והא דדייקינן אמתני' "בצמר אין, בפשתים לא" — בכיתנא רומאה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 61b:3:2.english: And this applies only to Roman flax - And that which we infer from the Mishnah, "[She must make thread] from wool — yes, from flax — no," [refers specifically] to Roman flax:

Tosafot on Ketubot 61b:4:1.hebrew: הלכה כר"א - והא דקי"ל בכ"מ ששנה רשב"ג במשנתנו הלכה כמותו — אין זה אותו שהיה בימי ר"א:
Tosafot on Ketubot 61b:4:1.english: "The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer" - And [regarding] that which we hold [as an established rule], that in every place where Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel taught in our Mishnah the halakha is like him — this [Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel to whom the rule applies] is not the same one who lived in the days of Rabbi Eliezer.

Tosafot on Ketubot 61b:7:1.hebrew: איכא בינייהו שפחות - אומר רשב"ם: שפחות ושכנגדה — דהיינו אפר מקלה, שהוא מימרא — דתרווייהו בינייהו נינהו. ור"ת פי', דהא דקאמר "מתני' ומתניתא רב מלכיא", לא אתא לאפלוגי על מימרא של רב מלכיא, אלא אתא למימר דכל מתני' ומתניתא רב מלכיא ולא רב מלכיו, אבל [שמעתתא יש מהם רב מלכיו ויש מהם] נמי רב מלכיא. וכן מוכח דקאמר "וסימניך מתניתא מלכתא", אבל משמעתתא לא נותן סימן:
Tosafot on Ketubot 61b:7:1.english: There is [a difference] between them [concerning] maidservants - Rashbam says: Maidservants and its counterpart — namely, kiln ash [efer makleh], which is an Amoraic statement [meimra] — both of them are [points of difference] between them. And Rabbeinu Tam explained that when [Rav Pappa] says, "A mishnah and a baraita [are by] Rav Malkiya," he does not come to dispute the Amoraic statement [meimra] of Rav Malkiya; rather, he comes to say that every mishnah and baraita is [by] Rav Malkiya and not Rav Malkiyyu, whereas [among Amoraic statements, some of them are by Rav Malkiyyu and some of them are] also [by] Rav Malkiya. And so it is proven, as he says, "And your mnemonic is: matnita malketa [the mishnah is a queen]," whereas for Amoraic statements [shema'tata] he does not give a mnemonic.
